Targeted Autoimmune Hair Loss Care
The Alopecia Areata Treatment
Alopecia areata is an autoimmune disorder that causes hair to come out, often in clumps the size and shape of a coin, as the immune system mistakenly attacks hair follicles. It can affect the scalp, beard, eyebrows, eyelashes, and other body areas, ranging from patchy areas (alopecia areata) to complete scalp hair loss (alopecia totalis) or total body hair loss (alopecia universalis).

ISAAC Luxe individualises treatment based on severity and response: corticosteroid injections administered directly into affected areas every 4–8 weeks to stimulate regrowth, topical minoxidil applied 2–3 times daily, topical corticosteroids applied to bald spots, and anthralin, which shows enhanced results when combined with minoxidil.

Treatment Approaches

Corticosteroid Injections

Administered directly into affected areas every 4–8 weeks.

Topical Minoxidil & Corticosteroids

Applied to bald spots to maintain and promote regrowth.

Anthralin

Enhanced results when combined with minoxidil.

What It Treats
Patchy Baldness Alopecia Totalis Alopecia Universalis Autoimmune Hair Loss

What to Expect
Your Treatment Journey
01

Consultation

Your dermatologist assesses your hair loss pattern and severity to select the right combination of treatments for you.

02

The Procedure

Depending on your plan, this may include corticosteroid injections directly into affected areas, topical minoxidil, topical corticosteroids, or anthralin application.

03

Aftercare

Topical treatments like minoxidil are applied 2–3 times daily; anthralin is washed off after the time recommended by your dermatologist.

04

Results Timeline

Corticosteroid injections are typically scheduled every 4–8 weeks, with your dermatologist adjusting your protocol based on your response over time.
